description: Weblitz, by SSRS2: HTML, CSS and JavaScript to PDF from a .NET library, printed as Chrome prints them: no browser to install or drive. Flexbox, grid, paged media (@page, margin boxes, page breaks), web fonts, SVG, and the page's scripts (React, Chart.js...) run once before printing. The same page also as an Excel workbook, a Word document, a PowerPoint deck or pictures (HtmlToExcel, HtmlToWord, HtmlToPowerPoint, HtmlToImage). .NET 8, 9, 10 and 11 on Windows, Linux and macOS. Licensed with SSRS2's licence key: one key for SSRS2's reports and Weblitz.
releaseNotes: 2.0.0-rc.1, the release candidate of 2.0: WeblitzPdf, SSRS2.NETCore, SSRS2.Mcp, the Node.js, Python and Java packages and the server images all at one version. Found by stress tests beside Chrome (hundreds of generated and hostile pages, live sites, a process printing 1,600 pages in a row): a picture shown as its alternative text in a pre-wrap container, and text holding half an emoji (a script's substring) under lowercase, capitalize, Greek uppercase, justification or ruby, no longer lose the PDF. On macOS a long-lived process no longer dies after a few hundred live pages: the engine no longer turns on .NET's Network.framework TLS for the whole process (an application that needs sites served over TLS 1.3 alone turns that switch on itself). An @page rule that leaves no page area prints with the default page box, as Chrome prints it. An SVG background repeated over an area is one pattern (2.6 times less memory), and one of more than 4,096 tiles is drawn (it was left out). Shrinking to fit counts an absolutely positioned box as large as its own transform makes it, and a headline whose size reads the viewport keeps it when the page shrinks (dropbox.com lost its last page). Header and footer templates are laid out once for all the pages of a paper size (5 ms to 0.16 ms a page), and a template wider than its page is cut as Chrome cuts it, no longer shrunk. A position: fixed box is painted once for all the printed pages (a long document under a heavy fixed panel takes a third of the time and memory, a fixed header's PDF a quarter of the size), and one placed above the window prints at the foot of each page but the last, as Chrome prints it. A script the page inserts runs between tasks that queue more without end (hashnode.com spun to 2 GB; it prints in 3.4 s). Pages built of many web components print faster (otto.de 16.3 s to 6.4 s): their style sheets are indexed once and shared, and a page restyles only what changed. A word of a million letters lays out in seconds where it took minutes, and pages of thousands of blank or scaled pages print in Chrome's page count without their work exploding. The page's clock, time zone, locale and Math.random are set in V8 itself. The script engine's linux-arm64 crash at exit is gone. 2.0.0-beta.10: pictures from HTML: HtmlToImage, beside HtmlToPdf and the Office classes with the same Render, RenderFile and RenderUrl: the whole page in one image as a screen shows it (Puppeteer's fullPage screenshot), the window alone, or each printed page as the PDF prints it; PNG, JPEG, WebP, or TIFF holding every page. The same page gives the same Word, Excel and PowerPoint file, byte for byte: their relationship ids are numbered and their files dated by the page's clock (they carried random ids and the time of the render). Word documents open as today's Word's, not in Compatibility Mode, with a cell's padding, CSS page breaks, a callout's borders and background, and an inline SVG as a picture. A page whose script navigates before the print (a language redirect, a bot check that sets a cookie and reloads, a form it submits, a refresh meta) is followed as Chrome's print follows it, five navigations at most, each held to the network options, with the render's own cookies; requests carry Chrome's headers, a script's fetch() and XMLHttpRequest the page's headers and credentials with Chrome's CORS preflight; the navigation API runs as in Chrome (Angular's router stays in its document). Pages that animate SVG print faster, only what changed styled again (swissinfo 23 s to 4 s, Le Figaro 10 s to 4 s, twilio.com stopped at the scripts' 30 s, now 5 s). A document whose footers say "Page N of M" is written while it is still laid out, its footers added once the count is known (1,000 letters 1,541 ms to 1,223 ms on 4 cores). SVG references and animations inside shadow trees resolve in their own tree. 2.0.0-beta.9: text set vertically (writing-mode: vertical-rl or vertical-lr) on a Mac: Chinese and Japanese ideographs go down the line by their font's vertical advance, as Chrome sets them. Since macOS 26 they come from PingFang SC, whose outlines are in a table of Apple's own, and each went 0 down the line: a column of Japanese drew its ideographs on top of each other. 2.0.0-beta.8: the Office files, as beta.7 wrote them from live pages. Every workbook passes the Open XML SDK's validation (its properties name its sheets). A table's pictures are in the workbook, over their cells where the page shows them (a country's flag beside its name). In Word, a menu the page lays out in a row is one line, not a page-long list. Pictures in AVIF, JPEG XL and SVG are in Word documents and workbooks (they were left out). A noscript's text and an SVG's title, which the page never shows, are no longer written as text (a news front page's workbook began with a style rule). On slides, a paragraph's lines are one text box, at the page's exact line spacing, and a table is a PowerPoint table: its columns and rows the page's, its cells' text where the page prints it, numbers flush right, the page's borders and backgrounds under it. 2.0.0-beta.7: a page out as an Office file, three classes beside HtmlToPdf with the same Render, RenderFile and RenderUrl. HtmlToExcel writes the page's data tables as a workbook, a sheet a table, numbers, percentages, amounts and ISO dates as typed cells. HtmlToWord writes the page as a document to edit: headings in Word's heading styles, paragraphs, lists, tables, pictures, links. HtmlToPowerPoint prints the page on slides (16:9 by default), a slide a printed page, its text as text boxes over one picture of the rest. Each has its own options, whose Page is the PDF's HtmlPdfOptions. First versions: tell us what your pages need. Also: a video's file is read up to its first picture and no longer whole, several videos at once (a news front page with three looping videos printed in 4 s where it took 30 s or more). 2.0.0-beta.6: on Alpine Linux, Weblitz runs with the gcompat package alone again (apk add --no-cache gcompat fontconfig): since the script engine's own build, a render there ended in a segmentation fault unless gcompat's library was preloaded; the engine now loads it itself, and says what to install where the package is missing. 2.0.0-beta.5: found by using beta.4 as a customer, on live addresses and in containers. Printing a live address is faster: the network's answers are no longer waited for one at a time, so a page of many small requests no longer reaches the scripts' limit (ten live sites printed with both versions, none slower; Le Monde's front page in 5.5 s where it took 18.8 s, Asahi's in 14.1 s where it took 32.7 s). On Linux, a missing fontconfig is reported with what to install (the official .NET Docker images lack libfontconfig1); a render failed in a type initializer. A process printing pages with shadow trees one after the other no longer keeps each finished document in memory. Consent = Hide outweighs the consent platforms' own rules: pages they cut to their first page print whole, and one printed under its veil prints clear. UpdateFilterListsAsync names each list's version. 2.0.0-beta.4: live pages checked beside Chrome (151 public pages): web fonts are fetched by unicode-range as Chrome fetches them, content-visibility: auto and lazy images load where Chrome's do, and the layout and print differences found on those pages are fixed. Pages that animate print faster: styles, layout and SVG icons are kept from one frame to the next where nothing changed for them, and a playing video's frame is decoded once. New options: Consent = Hide (consent boxes are left out, nothing is clicked), Ads = Block (advertisements and trackers are left out by the EasyList filter lists, shipped beside the assembly and updated with HtmlToPdf.UpdateFilterListsAsync), Automated (navigator.webdriver, true by default), UserAgent. 2.0.0-beta.3: a chart or any other canvas drawing prints on a page shrunk to fit its paper (it was left empty where the page's styles use viewport units: Chart.js's own documentation on A4). 2.0.0-beta.2: without a licence, the trial watermark runs across each page, as on reports (2.0.0-beta.1 drew it small in the page's top-left corner). 2.0.0-beta.1: the first beta of Weblitz, SSRS2's HTML engine. Details: https://ssrs2.net
title: Weblitz: HTML to PDF for .NET, by SSRS2
